(*
version 1.5	2. jan. 2012
programmer 	hugo
tested by	oscat

this function will insert a string at a given position in a buffer.
the function needs to be called:	_buffer_init(adr("array"),sizeof("array"),init);
this function will manipulate a given array.
the function manipulates the original array, it returnes the next position after the input string when finished.
because this function works with pointers its very time efficient and it needs no extra memory.

*)
FUNCTION _BUFFER_INSERT : INT
VAR_INPUT
	STR : STRING(STRING_LENGTH);
	POS : INT;
	PT : POINTER TO ARRAY[0..32767] OF BYTE;
	SIZE : UINT;
END_VAR
VAR
	end : INT;
	lx: INT;
	i: INT;
END_VAR
lx := LEN(str);
end := pos + lx;
(* first move the upper part of the buffer to make space for the string *)
FOR i := UINT_TO_INT(size) - 1 TO end BY -1 DO
	pt^[i] := pt^[i-lx];
END_FOR;
(* copy the string *)
_BUFFER_INSERT := _STRING_TO_BUFFER(str, pos, PT, size);

(*
version 2.0		21. mar. 2011
programmer 	hugo
tested by		kurt

LIST_ADD appends another element to the end of a list.
The list is represented as a string of elements, each starting with the character SEP.

*)
FUNCTION LIST_ADD : BOOL
VAR_INPUT
	SEP : BYTE;
	INS : STRING(LIST_LENGTH);
END_VAR

VAR
	sx : STRING(1);
END_VAR



(*All VAR_IN_OUT variables have been moved to the end of the declaration due to compatibility reasons*)
VAR_IN_OUT
	LIST : STRING(LIST_LENGTH);
END_VAR
sx := CHR_TO_STRING(SEP);			(* convert separation character to string *)
INS := CONCAT(sx, INS);					(* start element with separation character *)

IF LEN(LIST) + LEN(INS) > LIST_LENGTH THEN
	LIST_ADD := FALSE;					(* return false if element does not fit *)
ELSE
	LIST := CONCAT(LIST, INS);
	LIST_ADD := TRUE;
END_IF;


(* revision histroy

hm	21. mar. 2011	rev 2.0
	original release
*)
END_FUNCTION_BLOCK

LIST_CLEAN cleans a list of empty elements.
The list is represented as a string of elements, each starting with the character SEP.

*)
FUNCTION LIST_CLEAN : BOOL
VAR_INPUT
	SEP : BYTE;
END_VAR

VAR
	pt : POINTER TO ARRAY[1..LIST_LENGTH] OF BYTE;
	read : INT := 1;
	write : INT := 1;

(*All VAR_IN_OUT variables have been moved to the end of the declaration due to compatibility reasons*)
VAR_IN_OUT

pt := ADR(LIST);

FOR read := 1 TO LIST_LENGTH DO

(* value to be converted into a fraction *)
FUNCTION REAL_TO_FRAC : FRACTION
VAR_INPUT
	X : REAL;					
	N : INT;					(* maximum size of denominator *)
END_VAR
VAR
	temp : DINT;				(* marker for calculations *)

	sign: BOOL;					(* sign of the input value *)
	X_gerundet: DINT;			(* value of fraction, rounded to integer *)
	X_ohne_Nachkomma: REAL;		(* value of fraction, without decimal places *)
	Numerator:       DINT := 1;	(* initial value numerator  *)
	Denominator:     DINT := 0;	(* initial value denominator *)
	Numerator_old:   DINT := 0;	(* initial value numerator of last calculation  *)
	Denominator_old: DINT := 1;	(* initial value denominator of last calculation   *)

END_VAR

(*
version 1.1		06. apr. 2011
programmer 	alexander
tested by		hugo

this function calculates the closest fraction for a real number

*)
IF X < 0.0 THEN
	sign := TRUE;								(* remember sign *)
	X := ABS(X);								(* calculate absolute value *)
END_IF;

REPEAT
	X_gerundet := REAL_TO_DINT(X);

	(* calculate numerator *)
	temp := numerator * X_gerundet + numerator_old;		(* extend numerator by integer part *)
	numerator_old := numerator;							(* store numerator of last calculation *)
	numerator := temp;									(* store numerator of this calculation *)

	(* calculate denominator *)
	temp := denominator * X_gerundet + denominator_old;	(* extend denominator by integer part *)
	denominator_old := denominator;						(* store denominator of last calculation *)
	denominator := temp;								(* store denominator of this calculation *)

	(* calculate remainder *)
	X_ohne_Nachkomma := DINT_TO_REAL(X_gerundet);
	IF X = X_ohne_Nachkomma THEN						(* fraction is exact *)
		IF ABS(denominator) <= N THEN						(* no rounding error *)
			numerator_old := numerator;					(* numerator_old is returned by function *)
			denominator_old := denominator;			(* denominator_old is returned by function *)
		END_IF
		EXIT;											(* no further calculation necessary *)
	ELSE
		X := 1.0 / (X - X_ohne_Nachkomma);				(* reciprocal of remainder -> new fraction *)
	END_IF

UNTIL
	ABS(Denominator) > N
END_REPEAT

(* correct sign if X was negative *)
IF sign THEN
	REAL_TO_FRAC.NUMERATOR := -1 * ABS(DINT_TO_INT(numerator_old));
ELSE
	REAL_TO_FRAC.NUMERATOR :=  ABS(DINT_TO_INT(numerator_old));
END_IF
REAL_TO_FRAC.DENOMINATOR := ABS(DINT_TO_INT(denominator_old));

FUNCTION REAL_TO_STRF : STRING(20)
VAR_INPUT
	IN : REAL;
	N : INT;
	D : STRING(1);
END_VAR
VAR
	O: REAL;
	i: INT;

(* round the input to N digits and convert to string *)

REAL_TO_STRF := DINT_TO_STRING(REAL_TO_DINT(O));
(* add zeroes in front to make sure sting is at least 8 digits long *)
FOR i := LEN(REAL_TO_STRF) TO N DO REAL_TO_STRF := CONCAT('0', REAL_TO_STRF); END_FOR;
(* add a dot if n > 0 *)
IF n > 0 THEN REAL_TO_STRF := INSERT(REAL_TO_STRF, D, LEN(REAL_TO_STRF) - N); END_IF;
(* add a minus sign if in is negative *)
IF in < 0 THEN REAL_TO_STRF := CONCAT('-', REAL_TO_STRF); END_IF;

(*
version 1.5	24. jan. 2011
programmer 	hugo
tested by	oscat

this functions returns TRUE IF dst TIME is active
the FUNCTION calculates automatically for any year betweek 1970 AND 2099
wheather daylight savings is on OR off
the summertime calculation is done according to european standards.
dst will become TRUE AT 01:00 utc in the morning FOR the respective days
AND it will become FALSE after daylight savings TIME is switched back end OF october at 01:00 utc

*)
FUNCTION DST : BOOL
VAR_INPUT
	UTC : DT;
END_VAR
VAR
	yr : INT;
	yr4 : DWORD;
	ltc: DWORD;
	idate : DWORD;
END_VAR
yr := YEAR_OF_DATE(DT_TO_DATE(UTC));
ltc := DT_TO_DWORD(UTC);
idate := DT_TO_DWORD(SET_DT(yr, 3, 31, 1, 0, 0));
yr4 := SHR(5 * INT_TO_DWORD(yr), 2) + 1;
DST := (idate - ((yr4 + 3) MOD 7) * 86400 <= ltc) AND (idate + (214 - (yr4) MOD 7) * 86400 > ltc);

    * 28 October 2007
    * 26 October 2008

FUNCTION_BLOCK SUN_TIME
VAR_INPUT
	LATITUDE : REAL;				
	LONGITUDE : REAL;				(* longitude of geographical position  *)
	UTC : DATE;						(*	world time	*)
	H : REAL := -0.83333333333;	(* heighth above horizon for sunrise *)
END_VAR
VAR_OUTPUT
	MIDDAY : TOD;			(*	astrological midday in hours when sun stands at south direction	*)
	SUN_RISE : TOD;				(*	sun rise for current day in local time *)
	SUN_SET : TOD;				(*	sun set for current day in local time *)
	SUN_DECLINATION : REAL;		(*	sun declination above horizon at midday in degrees	*)
END_VAR
VAR
	dk: REAL;						(* sun declination at midday *)
	delta: TIME;					(* delta from midday for sunrise and sunset  *)
	b: REAL;
END_VAR

(*
version 1.7	25. jan. 2011
programmer 	hugo
tested by	tobias

this FUNCTION block calculates the sun rise, sun set, sun offset at midday sun declination for a given date
for performance reasons the algorithm has been simplified and is accurate within a few minutes only
the times are calculated in utc and have to be corrected for the given time zone
this correction is not done within sun_time because it would be a problem on days where dst is enabled or disabled

*)
B := latitude * 0.0174532925199433;
MIDDAY := SUN_MIDDAY(longitude, utc);
DK := 0.40954 * SIN(0.0172 * (INT_TO_REAL(DAY_OF_YEAR(utc)) - 79.35));
sun_declination := DEG(DK);
IF sun_declination > 180.0 THEN sun_declination := sun_declination - 360.0; END_IF;
sun_declination := 90.0 - LATITUDE + sun_declination;
delta := HOUR_TO_TIME(ACOS((SIN(RAD(H)) - SIN(B) * SIN(DK)) / (COS(B) * COS(DK))) * 3.819718632);
sun_rise := MIDDAY - delta;
sun_set := MIDDAY + delta;

ltime is a real time clock that uses the system rtc as utc time and calculates and given time zone.
the utc time is supplied on the input UTC.
according to the input variable time_zone_offset when the input dst_enable is true,
the dst on and off times are calculated by a formula for any given year and the time is advanced and reset by one hour
at 02:00 and 03:00 for the last sunday of march and last sunday of october.
the code is high performance and the rtc counts every second.
if more then one time zone is needed by the systen the clock can be started many times by placing more then one function block.

FUNCTION UTC_TO_LTIME : DT
VAR_INPUT
	UTC : DT;
	DST_ENABLE : BOOL;
	TIME_ZONE_OFFSET : INT;
END_VAR
VAR
	tmp: INT;
END_VAR
tmp := TIME_ZONE_OFFSET * 60 + BOOL_TO_INT(DST_ENABLE AND DST(UTC)) * 3600;
IF tmp < 0 THEN
	tmp := ABS(tmp);
	UTC_TO_LTIME := DWORD_TO_DT(DT_TO_DWORD(UTC) -  INT_TO_DWORD(tmp));
ELSE
	UTC_TO_LTIME := DWORD_TO_DT(DT_TO_DWORD(UTC) +  INT_TO_DWORD(tmp));
END_IF;

LINEAR_INT calculates an output based on a linear interpolation of up to 20 coordinates given in an array

*)
FUNCTION LINEAR_INT : REAL
VAR_INPUT
	X : REAL;
	XY : ARRAY[1..20,0..1] OF REAL;
	Pts : INT;
END_VAR
VAR
	i : INT;
END_VAR
(*make sure n is bound within the array size *)
pts := MIN(pts,20);

	below and above the defined segments we interpolate the last segment *)

	i := i + 1;

LINEAR_INT := ((XY[i,1] - XY[i-1,1]) * X - XY[i,1] * XY[i-1,0] + XY[i-1,1] * XY[i,0]) / (XY[i,0] - XY[i-1,0]);

this function checks a floating point variable of type real (IEEE754-32Bits) for NAN and infinity

*)
FUNCTION CHK_REAL : BYTE
VAR_INPUT
	X : REAL;
END_VAR
VAR
	pt : POINTER TO DWORD;
	tmp : DWORD;
END_VAR
pt := ADR(X);				(* move real to dword, real_to_dword does not work becasze it treats dword as a number on many systems *)
tmp := ROL(pt^,1);			(* rotate left foir easy checking, sign will be at lease significant digit *)
IF tmp < 16#FF000000 THEN
	CHK_REAL := 16#00;		(* normalized and denormalized numbers *)

	CHK_REAL := 16#20;		(* X is +infinity see IEEE754 *)
ELSIF tmp = 16#FF000001 THEN
	CHK_REAL := 16#40;		(* X is -infinity see IEEE754 *)
ELSE
	CHK_REAL := 16#80;		(* X is NAN see IEEE754 *)
END_IF;

CRC_GEN generates a CRC checksum from a block of data and returns  the checksum in a DWORD to be connected to the data for transmission.
the CRC Polynom is specified with the config variable PN and the length of the Polynom is specified by PL
A Polynom x4 + X + 1 is represented by 0011 with length 4, the highest order bit is not specified at all..
The input data is an array of byte of any size, the function is called by CRC_GEN(ADR(array),SIZEOF(array), ....).

*)
FUNCTION CRC_GEN : DWORD

VAR_INPUT
	PT : POINTER TO ARRAY[0..32000] OF BYTE;
	SIZE : INT;
	PL : INT;
	PN : DWORD;
	INIT : DWORD;
	REV_IN : BOOL;
	REV_OUT : BOOL;
	XOR_OUT : DWORD;
END_VAR
VAR
	pos : INT;
	shift : INT;
	dx: BYTE;
	bits: INT;
END_VAR
(* align polynomial *)
shift := 32 - PL;
PN := SHL(PN, shift);

(* load first 4 bytes into register minimum message size is 4 bytes
	for smaller messages fill with 0#s at the beginning*)
FOR pos := 0 TO 3 DO
	IF REV_IN THEN CRC_GEN := SHL(CRC_GEN, 8) OR REVERSE(PT^[pos]); ELSE CRC_GEN := SHL(CRC_GEN, 8) OR PT^[pos]; END_IF;
END_FOR;
pos := 4;

(* xor with init value *)
CRC_GEN := CRC_GEN XOR SHL(init, shift);

(* calculate CRC for each byte *)
WHILE pos < size DO
	IF REV_IN THEN DX := REVERSE(PT^[pos]); ELSE DX := PT^[pos]; END_IF;
	pos := pos + 1;
	(* crc calculation for one byte *)
	FOR bits := 0 TO 7 DO
		IF CRC_GEN.31 THEN
			CRC_GEN := (SHL(CRC_GEN, 1) OR BOOL_TO_DWORD(DX.7)) XOR PN;
		ELSE
			CRC_GEN := SHL(CRC_GEN, 1) OR BOOL_TO_DWORD(DX.7);
		END_IF;
		dx := SHL(dx, 1);
	END_FOR;
END_WHILE;

(* all bytes are processed, need to finish the registers 32 bits *)
FOR bits := 0 TO 31 DO
	IF CRC_GEN.31 THEN
		CRC_GEN := (SHL(CRC_GEN, 1) ) XOR PN;
	ELSE
		CRC_GEN := SHL(CRC_GEN, 1);
	END_IF;
END_FOR;

(* final XOR *)
CRC_GEN := SHR(CRC_GEN, shift) XOR XOR_OUT;

(* reverse the crc_output if necessary *)
IF REV_OUT THEN CRC_GEN := REFLECT(CRC_GEN, PL); END_IF;

(* suggested optimization by deninis klopke
The mentioned function can be optimized as follows:
In lines 33 and 35 of the implementation part, the part OR BOOL_TO_DWORD(DX.7) can be omitted, since after 8 left shifts of DX in line 26 the value of DX = BYTE#0. A further OR with this value has no effect on the result.
*)

(* typical crc polynomials

CRC-4-ITU 			x4 + x + 1 					(ITU G.704, p. 12) 	0x3 or 0xC (0x9)
CRC-5-ITU 			x5 + x4 + x2 + 1 			(ITU G.704, p. 9) 	0x15 or 0x15 (0x0B) Bluetooth
CRC-5-USB 			x5 + x2 + 1 				(use: USB token packets) 	0x05 or 0x14 (0x9)
CRC-6-ITU 			x6 + x + 1 					(ITU G.704, p. 3) 	0x03 or 0x30 (0x21)
CRC-7 				x7 + x3 + 1 				(use: telecom systems, MMC) 	0x09 or 0x48 (0x11)
CRC-8-ATM 			x8 + x2 + x + 1 				(use: ATM HEC) 	0x07 or 0xE0 (0xC1)

CRC-16-CCITT 	x16 + x12 + x5 + 1 (XMODEM,X.25, V.41, Bluetooth, PPP, IrDA; known as "CRC-CCITT") 	0x1021 or 0x8408 (0x0811)
CRC-16-IBM 	x16 + x15 + x2 + 1 (USB, many others; also known as "CRC-16") 	0x8005 or 0xA001 (0x4003)

CRC-64-ISO 	x64 + x4 + x3 + x + 1 (use: ISO 3309) 	0x000000000000001B or 0xD800000000000000 (0xB000000000000001)

(as described in ECMA-182 p.63) 	0x42F0E1EBA9EA3693 or 0xC96C5795D7870F42 (0x92D8AF2BAF0E1E85)

(* This PID controller implements an integrator anti-windup method (back-calculation).
For this the difference between the unlimited control output the limited control output is added to the integrator input.
This is done continously, allowing to track and correct the gain of the integrator.
*)
FUNCTION_BLOCK FB_PID

VAR_INPUT
	xSet:	REAL; 	// Set value
	xAct:	REAL;	// measured Value

	Kp  :  	REAL;  	// proportional factor
	Ti  :  	REAL;  	// integral time
	Td  :	REAL; 	// derivative time
	Ni  :	REAL := 0.9; 	// time for anti-wiundup compensation

	LimLow	:	REAL; 	// lower limit of output
	LimHigh	: 	REAL; 	// upper limit of output
	StartY	:	REAL;	// Y to use as offset

	bReverseActing 	:	BOOL;	// True for reverse acting

	RST		:	BOOL; 	// True, if integrator should be resetted
	inStart	:	REAL := 0; 	// Value to which Integrator is resetted if RST is True
END_VAR
VAR_OUTPUT
	Y : REAL;		// controller output
	LIM : BOOL;		// True, if output reaches LimLow or LimHigh
END_VAR
VAR
	e			 :  REAL;		// control difference
	yOffset		 :  REAL	:= 0;		// constant offset used on Y
	fbDerivative :  FT_DERIV; 	// function block for derivation
	fbIntegrate  :	FB_Integrate;	// function block for integration

	e_gaintrack	:  REAL;		// control difference for integrator
	Y_gaintrack	:  REAL := 0;	// tracking gain of y for Anti-windup
END_VAR
IF StartY <> yOffset THEN
	yOffset := StartY;
	fbIntegrate(RST:=TRUE, inStart:=inStart);
END_IF
IF RST THEN
	fbIntegrate(RST:=TRUE, inStart:=inStart);
END_IF

//determine direct or reverse acting
IF bReverseActing THEN
	e := xAct - xSet;
ELSE
	e := xSet - xAct;
END_IF;

// correct control for integrator error based on previous integrations
e_gaintrack := e + Y_gaintrack/(Kp*Ni);

IF Ti>0 THEN
	//derivative and integral calculation
	fbDerivative(in:=e,run:=TRUE);
	fbIntegrate(run:= TRUE, in := e_gaintrack, RST:=RST);
	Y := Kp * (e + 1/Ti * fbIntegrate.out + Td * fbDerivative.out) + yOffset;
ELSE
	//derivative  calculation
	fbDerivative(in:=e,run:=TRUE);
	Y := Kp * (e + Td * fbDerivative.out) + yOffset;
END_IF

// check limits and track gain for adjusting next control error of integrator
IF Y < LimLow THEN
	Y_gaintrack := LimLow - Y;
	Y := LimLow;
ELSIF Y > LimHigh THEN
	Y_gaintrack := LimHigh - Y;
	Y := LimHigh;
ELSE
	Y_gaintrack := 0;
END_IF


(*
fse 17.10.2023:
- adjust anti-windup according to AixLib implementation

pos 23.10.2020:
- no anti-wind up on reset
- possibility to provide an offset value for Y

aku 24.09.2019:
- first implementation
*)

	T : TIME;
	K : REAL := 1.0;
END_VAR
VAR_OUTPUT
	out : REAL;
END_VAR
VAR
	last : DWORD;
	tx: DWORD;
	init: BOOL;
END_VAR
(* read system time *)
tx := T_PLC_US();

(* startup initialisation *)
IF NOT init OR T = t#0s THEN
	init := TRUE;
	out := K * in;
ELSE
	out := out + (in * K - out) * DWORD_TO_REAL(Tx - last) / TIME_TO_REAL(T) * 1.0E-3;
	IF ABS(out) < 1.0E-20 THEN out := 0.0; END_IF;
END_IF;
last := tx;

Calibrate allows for offset and scale calibration of an analog input.
offset is calibrated to a stored reference Y_offset while CO is true.
after the offset is calibrated, scale can be calibrated to a reference value Y_scale while CS is true.
*)
FUNCTION_BLOCK CALIBRATE
VAR_INPUT
	X : REAL;
	CO : BOOL;
	CS : BOOL;
END_VAR
VAR_INPUT CONSTANT
	Y_Offset : REAL;
	Y_Scale : REAL;
END_VAR
VAR_OUTPUT

VAR RETAIN
	offset : REAL;
	Scale : REAL := 1.0;
END_VAR

IF CO THEN
	OFFSET := Y_Offset - X;
ELSIF CS THEN
	SCALE := Y_scale / (X + OFFSET);
END_IF;
(* calculate output *)
Y := (X + OFFSET) * SCALE;

(*
version 1.2	16. nov 2008
programmer 	hugo
tested by	oscat

T_PLC_MS reads the internal PLC timer and return the time, it has the advantage to be able to set a debug mode
and speed up the counter to test the plc timer overrun which occurs every 50 days respectively 25 days at siemens S7
this routine also allows to correct the behavior of s7 where the internal plc counter will not count all 32 bits.

*)
FUNCTION T_PLC_MS : DWORD
VAR CONSTANT
	debug : BOOL := 0;
	N : INT := 0;
	offset : DWORD := 0;
END_VAR
VAR
	tx : TIME;
END_VAR
tx := TIME();
T_PLC_MS := TIME_TO_DWORD(Tx);
(* Here, the correction for Step7 must take place
plctime must use the full value range of time:
if, in Step7, time is from -24 days to +24 days, then the timer must also jump to -24 days on overflow
and under no circumstances to 0!!!!
for Siemens, another FB must be integrated in the main program to ensure that all 32 bits are counted.
It can only be one FB because it must remember the highest (32nd) bit.
Or does S7 jump to -24 days on overflow????? Then no correction would be necessary.
*)
IF debug THEN
	T_PLC_MS := (SHL(T_PLC_MS,N) OR SHL(DWORD#1,N)-1) + OFFSET;
END_IF;

	original version

hm	12. nov 2007	rev 1.1
	added temporaray variable tx because some compilers could not handle time() as an argument

	initialized constants with 0 for compatibility reasons

(*

this soft on/off ramp generator generates a soft on and soft off ramp while the max on value is set by the input
the time for a full ramp can be set by config variables for up and down ramp.

*)
FUNCTION_BLOCK RMP_SOFT
VAR_INPUT
	IN : BOOL;
	VAL : BYTE;
END_VAR
VAR_INPUT CONSTANT
	PT_ON: TIME;
	PT_OFF : TIME;
END_VAR
VAR_OUTPUT
	OUT : BYTE;
END_VAR
VAR
	rmp : _RMP_B;
	tmp: BYTE;
END_VAR
tmp := SEL(in, 0, val);
IF tmp > out THEN
	(* we need to ramp down *)
	rmp(dir := TRUE, E := TRUE, TR := PT_ON, rmp := out);
	(* make sure out does not surpass tmp *)
	out := MIN(out, tmp);
ELSIF tmp < out THEN
	(* we need to ramp up *)
	rmp(dir := FALSE, E := TRUE, TR := PT_OFF, rmp := out);
	(* make sure out does not surpass tmp *)
	out := MAX(out, tmp);
ELSE
	(* no ramp necessary *)
	rmp(E := FALSE, rmp := out);
END_IF;

Write a complete, production-ready Beckhoff TwinCAT 3 ST implementation for a module called 'AOUT'. Include all VAR declarations and deterministic industrial logic.

(*
version 1.4	23 feb 2008
programmer 	oscat
tested by		tobias

this module conditions an internal real value for D/A converter.
Aout converts and internal real value to a word for an D/A converter or other output devices.
The input value is converted to a n-bit wide output and a sign bit is set separately as specified.
the output min value is set for the specified min input value and the max output is set for the max input value.
an input higher or lower than the max or min value will set the respective max or min value of the output.


*)
FUNCTION AOUT : DWORD
VAR_INPUT
	in : REAL;
END_VAR
VAR_INPUT CONSTANT
	Bits : BYTE;
	sign : BYTE := 255;
	low : REAL;
	high : REAL := 10.0;
END_VAR
VAR CONSTANT
	ff : DWORD := 2#1;
END_VAR
VAR
	in2 : REAL;
	sx : BOOL;
END_VAR
(* if sign bit is defined *)
IF sign < 32 THEN
	sx := sign_R(in);
	in2 := ABS(in);
ELSE
	in2 := in;
END_IF;

(* limit in to the allowed values *)
in2 := LIMIT(low, in2, high);

(* calculate the output value *)
Aout := REAL_TO_DWORD((in2 - low) / (high - low) * DWORD_TO_REAL(SHL(ff,bits) -1));
IF sx THEN Aout := SHL(ff,sign) OR Aout; END_IF;

inputs ramp between min and max values for the respective inputs to be between (0..255).
the summed output is then scaled by an scale input K and a offset O can be added to the output.
min and max input configurations can be edited in the cfc editor by double clicking the symbol body.

*)
FUNCTION SCALE_B2 : REAL
VAR_INPUT
	in1: BYTE;
	in2: BYTE;
	K : REAL;
	O : REAL;
END_VAR
VAR_INPUT CONSTANT
	in1_min: REAL;
	in1_max: REAL := 1000.0;
	in2_min: REAL;
	in2_max: REAL := 1000.0;
END_VAR
SCALE_B2 := 	(((in1_max - in1_min)* in1 + (in2_max - in2_min)* in2) * 0.003921569 + in1_min + in2_min) * K + O;

FUNCTION SCALE_D : REAL
VAR_INPUT

(*
version 1.4	10. mar. 2009
programmer 	hugo
tested by		oscat

the function stair2 converts an anlog input signal to a staircase like output.
D is the step width for the output signal. the output will use D as a hysteresis for a stairchange.
if D = 0 then the output follows the input without a chage.
*)
FUNCTION_BLOCK STAIR2
VAR_INPUT
	X : REAL;
	D : REAL;
END_VAR
VAR_OUTPUT
	Y: REAL;
END_VAR
IF D > 0.0 THEN
	IF X >= Y + D OR X <= Y - D THEN Y := FLOOR(X/D) * D; END_IF;
ELSE
	Y := X;
END_IF;

    inIndex: INT; //Declara la variable de indice del array para el acceso indirecto
    xNewVal: BOOL; //Indica que hay una nueva lectura del sensor de fuerza.
    rFuerza: REAL; //Valor de fuerza del sensor.

VAR 
    stRectangulo1 : st_Rectangulo; // Estructura que contiene los datos del rectangulo1 A, B y su area
    stRectangulo2 : st_Rectangulo; // Estructura que contiene los datos del rectangulo2 A, B y su area

END_FOR;                      // Se incrementa inIndex y se repite el proceso.

// Ejemplo02: Creamos un FIFO en el que guardamos un valor analógico de fuera a cada impulso de la señal xNewVal.
IF xNewVal THEN                // Si hay un nuevo valor de fuerza realizamos el codigo.
    xNewVal := FALSE;          // Reset de la señal xNewVal.

    FOR inIndex:=20 TO 2 BY -1 DO // Variable indice a 20, hasta 2.
        aR20[inIndex] := aR20[inIndex-1]; //Desplazamiento de los valores en el FIFO --->
    END_FOR;                             // Se decrementa inIndex y se repite el proceso.

    aR20[1] := rFuerza; // Entrada del valor de fuerza en el primer elemento del FIFO.

stRectangulo1.rBside := 32; //Valor del lado B.

stRectangulo2.rBside := 320.4; //Valor del lado B.

stRectangulo3.rBside := 2048.4; //Valor del lado B.

stRectangulo1.rArea := Fc_AreaCalcVal(i_rAside:=stRectangulo1.rAside, i_rBside:= stRectangulo1.rBside);

// Cálculo del área del rectángulo pasando un puntero a la función
Fc_AreaCalcPoint(ADR(stRectangulo2));

Fc_AreaCalcRef(refRectangulo);

PROGRAM SR_Main_02

    in01    : INT; //Declaración de la variable in01 de tipo entero.

// Ejemplo de uso básico de los operadores ADR y del operador de contenido ^
// Se muestra como asignar a un puntero la dirección de memoria de una variable y como leer/escribir
// así como un ejemplo de acceso a variables locales de otros programas.

pint^ := 44;     //A la posición de memoria indicada por el puntero, le asignamos el valor 44

in03 := pint^; // in03 tomara el valor del contenido de la posición de memoria contenida en el
               // que hemos asignado la dirección de in02, por tanto in03= 123.

pint^ := 240 ; // La varible local del programa SR_Main_01.inLocalAway tomará el valor 240

PROGRAM SR_Main_04
VAR
 arFIFO  : ARRAY[1..20] OF REAL; // FIFO con los valores de fuerza registrados.
 intIdx  : INT;                  // Variable de indice.
 rIncAng : REAL;                 // Valor de incremento angular para generación de senoide.
 rValAng : REAL;                 // Valor actual de angulo.
 rValSin : REAL;                 // Amplitud de la senoide superpuesta.
 rVMed   : REAL;                 // Resultado del cálculo.

 refFIFO : REFERENCE TO ARRAY[1..20] OF REAL := arFIFO; // Crea una referencia y la asigna a arFIFO
 rMedRef : REAL;           // Resultado del cálculo para el ejemplo de pase de valores por Ref.
END_VAR
// Ejemplo de como realizar el cálculo del valor medio de las lecturas de fuerza contenidas en arFIFO
// mediante la función Fc_AverageValues (Pase de parámetros por valores) y Fc_AverageReferencia (Pase de
// parámetros por referencia)
// Lo que se pretende es ver las ventajas del pase por referencia

// Asignación de valores para llenar el FIFO a efectos de tener algunos valores para el cálculo de la media
// al valor 124 le superpone una variación senoidal de amplitud 6

rIncAng := (2 * 3.14159) / 20.0; // 2 * PI Radianes dividido entre 20 puntos.
rValAng := 0.0;                   // Valor inicial del angulo.

FOR intIdx :=1 TO 20 BY 1 DO
 rValSin := SIN(rValAng) * 6;         // Valor del seno para una amplitud de 6
 arFIFO[intIdx] := 124.0 + rValSin;  // A un nivel de 124.0 se superpone un seno de amplitud 6.
 rValAng := rValAng + rIncAng;       // Próximo valor angular. 
END_FOR;

// Con el FIFO de valores llamaremos a la función para el cálculo de la media pasando valores.
// Lo que no sería para nada adecuado por tratarse de muchos parámetros.

rVMed:= Fc_AverageValues( i_REALV1  := arFIFO[1],
                          i_REALV2  := arFIFO[2],
                          i_REALV3  := arFIFO[3],
                          i_REALV4  := arFIFO[4], 
                          i_REALV5  := arFIFO[5],
                          i_REALV6  := arFIFO[6], 
                          i_REALV7  := arFIFO[7],
                          i_REALV8  := arFIFO[8],
                          i_REALV9  := arFIFO[9],
                          i_REALV10 := arFIFO[10],
                          i_REALV11 := arFIFO[11],
                          i_REALV12 := arFIFO[12],
                          i_REALV13 := arFIFO[13],
                          i_REALV14 := arFIFO[14],
                          i_REALV15 := arFIFO[15],
                          i_REALV16 := arFIFO[16],
                          i_REALV17 := arFIFO[17],
                          i_REALV18 := arFIFO[18],
                          i_REALV19 := arFIFO[19],
                          i_REALV20 := arFIFO[20]);

// Con el FIFO lleno de valores llamaremos a la función para el cálculo de la media pasando valores por referencia
// para ver lo sencillo que resulta en este caso.

rMedRef := Fc_AverageReferencia(i_Ref:=refFIFO);
END_FUNCTION_BLOCK

METHOD PRIVATE State : E_Motor_State

VAR
    nextState : E_Motor_State;
END_VAR

nextState := _stMotor.State;
IF oAlertIsActive THEN
    nextState := E_Motor_State.Fault;
ELSE
    CASE _stMotor.State OF

        E_Motor_State.Stopped:
            IF oRunCommand THEN
                nextState := E_Motor_State.Starting;
            END_IF

        E_Motor_State.Starting:
            IF _stMotor.IO.Feedback THEN
                nextState := E_Motor_State.Running;
            END_IF

        E_Motor_State.Running:
            IF NOT oRunCommand THEN
                nextState := E_Motor_State.Stopping;
            END_IF

        E_Motor_State.Stopping:
            IF NOT _stMotor.IO.Feedback THEN
                nextState := E_Motor_State.Stopped;
            END_IF

        E_Motor_State.Fault:
            // Recovery only when fully stopped and de-energized
            IF NOT oRunCommand AND NOT _stMotor.IO.Feedback THEN
                nextState := E_Motor_State.Stopped;
            END_IF
    END_CASE
END_IF

FUNCTION fun_CommainCase : BOOL
VAR_INPUT
    (* Byte to be evaluated as a printable character. *)
    character : BYTE;
END_VAR

CASE character OF
    (*
    Any character that falls in the ascii range (in base-10)
    0-8, 11, 12, 14-27 or >=127 is an invalid character.
    *)
    BYTE#9..BYTE#10, BYTE#13, BYTE#28..BYTE#126:
        fun_CommainCase := TRUE;
ELSE
    fun_CommainCase := FALSE;
END_CASE
END_FUNCTION

(* =============================================================
   FB_SolenoidValve — Solenoid Valve Controller

   Category:     Actuators
   Platform:     CODESYS V3.5 (IEC 61131-3)
   Version:      1.0
   Dependencies: None (standard IEC only)

   Controls a normally-closed or normally-open solenoid valve
   with optional position feedback sensor and stuck-valve detection.

   Usage:
     fbValve : FB_SolenoidValve;
     fbValve(bOpen := bCmdOpenValve, bFeedback := bDI_ValveOpen,
             tFeedbackDelay := T#2S);
     bValveIsOpen := fbValve.bIsOpen;
   ============================================================= *)
FUNCTION_BLOCK FB_SolenoidValve
VAR_INPUT
    bOpen           : BOOL;                (* Command: open valve *)
    bFeedback       : BOOL;                (* Feedback sensor: valve open *)
    bUseFeedback    : BOOL := FALSE;       (* Enable feedback monitoring *)
    tFeedbackDelay  : TIME := T#2S;        (* Feedback timeout *)
    bNormallyOpen   : BOOL := FALSE;       (* TRUE=NO valve, FALSE=NC valve *)
    bEnable         : BOOL := TRUE;        (* Enable control *)
    bReset          : BOOL;                (* Reset error *)
END_VAR
VAR_OUTPUT
    bSolenoid       : BOOL;                (* Solenoid output *)
    bIsOpen         : BOOL;                (* Valve is open *)
    bIsClosed       : BOOL;                (* Valve is closed *)
    bErr          : BOOL;                (* Stuck valve error *)
    nErrId          : DINT;                 (* 0=OK, 1=Stuck open, 2=Stuck closed *)
END_VAR
VAR
    tonFeedback     : TON;
    bExpectedState  : BOOL;
END_VAR

IF bReset THEN
    bErr := FALSE;
    nErrId := 0;
    tonFeedback(IN := FALSE, PT := tFeedbackDelay);
END_IF

IF NOT bEnable THEN
    bSolenoid := bNormallyOpen;  (* De-energize = safe state *)
    bIsOpen := bNormallyOpen;
    bIsClosed := NOT bNormallyOpen;
    RETURN;
END_IF

(* Drive solenoid *)
IF bNormallyOpen THEN
    bSolenoid := NOT bOpen;  (* Energize to close *)
ELSE
    bSolenoid := bOpen;      (* Energize to open *)
END_IF

(* Status *)
IF bUseFeedback THEN
    bIsOpen := bFeedback;
    bIsClosed := NOT bFeedback;

    (* Stuck detection *)
    bExpectedState := bOpen;
    IF bFeedback <> bExpectedState THEN
        tonFeedback(IN := TRUE, PT := tFeedbackDelay);
        IF tonFeedback.Q AND NOT bErr THEN
            bErr := TRUE;
            IF bOpen AND NOT bFeedback THEN
                nErrId := 2; (* Stuck closed *)
            ELSE
                nErrId := 1; (* Stuck open *)
            END_IF
        END_IF
    ELSE
        tonFeedback(IN := FALSE, PT := tFeedbackDelay);
    END_IF
ELSE
    bIsOpen := bOpen;
    bIsClosed := NOT bOpen;
END_IF

END_FUNCTION_BLOCK

    (* Temperature feedback *)
    rActTemp            : REAL;             (* Actual tank temperature [deg C] *)
    rSetpoint           : REAL := 25.0;     (* Target temperature [deg C] *)
    (* Thermostat parameters *)
    rHysteresis         : REAL := 2.0;      (* Hysteresis band [deg C] *)
    rMaxTemp            : REAL := 40.0;     (* Max allowed temperature [deg C] *)
    rMinTemp            : REAL := 5.0;      (* Freeze protection threshold [deg C] *)
    (* Safety *)
    bLevelOK            : BOOL := TRUE;     (* Tank level OK — prevent dry running *)
    tMaxOnTime          : TIME := T#30M;    (* Max continuous heater ON time *)
END_VAR
VAR_OUTPUT
    bHeaterElement      : BOOL;             (* Heater output *)
    bHeating            : BOOL;             (* Heating in progress *)
    bTemperatureOK      : BOOL;             (* Temperature within range *)
    bOverheatAlarm      : BOOL;             (* Over-temperature alarm *)
    bFreezeAlarm        : BOOL;             (* Under-temperature alarm *)
    bTimeoutAlarm       : BOOL;             (* Max ON time exceeded *)
END_VAR
VAR
    bThermostatReq      : BOOL;             (* Internal thermostat state *)
    tonMaxTime          : TON;              (* Max ON timer *)
    tonOverheat         : TON;              (* Overheat confirmation *)
END_VAR

IF NOT bEnable THEN
    bHeaterElement := FALSE;
    bHeating := FALSE;
    bTemperatureOK := TRUE;
    bOverheatAlarm := FALSE;
    bFreezeAlarm := FALSE;
    bTimeoutAlarm := FALSE;
    RETURN;
END_IF;

(* ============================================================
   THERMOSTAT LOGIC WITH HYSTERESIS
   ============================================================ *)

(* Turn ON below setpoint - hysteresis *)
IF rActTemp < (rSetpoint - rHysteresis) THEN
    bThermostatReq := TRUE;
END_IF;

(* Turn OFF above setpoint + hysteresis *)
IF rActTemp > (rSetpoint + rHysteresis) THEN
    bThermostatReq := FALSE;
END_IF;

(* ============================================================
   SAFETY CHECKS
   ============================================================ *)

(* Overheat detection — confirmed after 5s *)
tonOverheat(IN := rActTemp > rMaxTemp, PT := T#5S);
bOverheatAlarm := tonOverheat.Q;

(* Freeze protection — always heat if too cold *)
bFreezeAlarm := rActTemp < rMinTemp;

(* Maximum continuous runtime *)
tonMaxTime(IN := bHeaterElement, PT := tMaxOnTime);
bTimeoutAlarm := tonMaxTime.Q;

(* ============================================================
   OUTPUT LOGIC
   ============================================================ *)

(* Heater ON conditions:
   1. Enabled AND commanded on (or freeze protection)
   2. Thermostat requests heat (or freeze protection)
   3. Water level OK (prevent dry-run)
   4. No overheat
   5. Max time not exceeded *)
bHeaterElement := bEnable AND
                  (bTurnOn OR bFreezeAlarm) AND
                  (bThermostatReq OR bFreezeAlarm) AND
                  bLevelOK AND
                  NOT bOverheatAlarm AND
                  NOT bTimeoutAlarm;

bHeating := bHeaterElement;

(* Temperature status *)
bTemperatureOK := (rActTemp >= rMinTemp) AND (rActTemp <= rMaxTemp);

END_FUNCTION_BLOCK

(* =============================================================
   FB_AxisScaler — Axis Unit Conversion (mm/pulses, mm-s/Hz)

   Category:     Motion
   Platform:     CODESYS V3.5 (IEC 61131-3)
   Version:      1.0
   Dependencies: None (standard IEC only)

   Converts between user units (mm, degrees) and machine units
   (encoder pulses, frequency Hz). Handles gear ratio and
   lead screw pitch calculations.

   Usage:
     fbScaler : FB_AxisScaler;
     fbScaler(rPitch := 5.0, nPulsesPerRev := 10000, rGearRatio := 1.0);
     nPulses := fbScaler.fnPosToPulses(rPositionMm := 100.0);
     rMm     := fbScaler.fnPulsesToPos(nPulses := 200000);
   ============================================================= *)
FUNCTION_BLOCK FB_AxisScaler
VAR_INPUT
    rPitch          : REAL := 5.0;         (* Lead screw pitch [mm/rev] or [deg/rev] *)
    nPulsesPerRev   : DINT := 10000;       (* Encoder pulses per revolution *)
    rGearRatio      : REAL := 1.0;         (* Gear ratio (motor/load) *)
END_VAR
VAR_OUTPUT
    rMmPerPulse     : REAL;                (* Conversion factor: mm per pulse *)
    rPulsesPerMm    : REAL;                (* Conversion factor: pulses per mm *)
END_VAR

(* Calculate conversion factors *)
IF nPulsesPerRev > 0 AND ABS(rGearRatio) > 0.0001 THEN
    rMmPerPulse := rPitch / (DINT_TO_REAL(nPulsesPerRev) * rGearRatio);
    IF ABS(rMmPerPulse) > 0.0 THEN
        rPulsesPerMm := 1.0 / rMmPerPulse;
    ELSE
        rPulsesPerMm := 0.0;
    END_IF
ELSE
    rMmPerPulse := 0.0;
    rPulsesPerMm := 0.0;
END_IF

END_FUNCTION_BLOCK

(* =============================================================
   FB_AnalogInput — Generic Analog Input with Scaling and Filtering

   Category:     Sensors
   Platform:     CODESYS V3.5 (IEC 61131-3)
   Version:      1.0
   Dependencies: None (standard IEC only)

   General-purpose analog input block with linear scaling from
   raw ADC to engineering units, first-order filtering, and
   high/low alarm limits.

   Usage:
     fbPressure : FB_AnalogInput;
     fbPressure(nRawValue := nAD_Ch1,
                rScaleMin := 0.0, rScaleMax := 10.0,
                sUnit := 'bar');
     rPressure := fbPressure.rValue;
   ============================================================= *)
FUNCTION_BLOCK FB_AnalogInput
VAR_INPUT
    nRawValue       : INT;                 (* Raw ADC value *)
    rScaleMin       : REAL := 0.0;         (* Engineering minimum *)
    rScaleMax       : REAL := 100.0;       (* Engineering maximum *)
    nRawMin         : INT := 0;            (* ADC raw minimum *)
    nRawMax         : INT := 32767;        (* ADC raw maximum *)
    rAlarmHigh      : REAL := 90.0;        (* High alarm limit *)
    rAlarmLow       : REAL := 5.0;         (* Low alarm limit *)
    rHysteresis     : REAL := 2.0;         (* Alarm hysteresis *)
    rFilterFactor   : REAL := 0.2;         (* Filter alpha (0.0-1.0) *)
    bEnable         : BOOL := TRUE;        (* Enable processing *)
END_VAR
VAR_OUTPUT
    rValue          : REAL;                (* Scaled value *)
    rPercent        : REAL;                (* 0-100% of scale *)
    bAlarmHigh      : BOOL;                (* High alarm *)
    bAlarmLow       : BOOL;                (* Low alarm *)
    bValid          : BOOL;                (* Reading valid *)
END_VAR
VAR
    rFiltered       : REAL;
    rRange          : REAL;
    bInit           : BOOL := FALSE;
END_VAR

IF NOT bEnable THEN
    bValid := FALSE;
    RETURN;
END_IF

(* Filter *)
IF NOT bInit THEN
    rFiltered := INT_TO_REAL(nRawValue);
    bInit := TRUE;
ELSE
    rFiltered := rFiltered + rFilterFactor * (INT_TO_REAL(nRawValue) - rFiltered);
END_IF

(* Scale *)
rRange := INT_TO_REAL(nRawMax - nRawMin);
IF ABS(rRange) > 0.001 THEN
    rValue := (rFiltered - INT_TO_REAL(nRawMin)) / rRange
              * (rScaleMax - rScaleMin) + rScaleMin;
    rPercent := (rFiltered - INT_TO_REAL(nRawMin)) / rRange * 100.0;
ELSE
    rValue := rScaleMin;
    rPercent := 0.0;
END_IF
bValid := TRUE;

(* Alarms with hysteresis *)
IF rValue >= rAlarmHigh THEN
    bAlarmHigh := TRUE;
ELSIF rValue < (rAlarmHigh - rHysteresis) THEN
    bAlarmHigh := FALSE;
END_IF

IF rValue <= rAlarmLow THEN
    bAlarmLow := TRUE;
ELSIF rValue > (rAlarmLow + rHysteresis) THEN
    bAlarmLow := FALSE;
END_IF

END_FUNCTION_BLOCK

(* =============================================================
   FB_FlowSensor — Flow Rate Sensor with Totalization

   Category:     Sensors
   Platform:     CODESYS V3.5 (IEC 61131-3)
   Version:      1.0
   Dependencies: None (standard IEC only)

   Monitors flow rate from analog sensor (4-20mA/0-10V).
   Includes low-flow alarm, totalization (accumulated volume),
   and peak flow tracking.

   Usage:
     fbFlow : FB_FlowSensor;
     fbFlow(nRawValue := nAD_Flow,
            rScaleMin := 0.0, rScaleMax := 50.0,
            rAlarmLow := 5.0, tCycleTime := T#100MS);
     rFlowRate  := fbFlow.rValue;
     rTotalVol  := fbFlow.rTotalVolume;
     bNoFlow    := fbFlow.bAlarmLow;
   ============================================================= *)
FUNCTION_BLOCK FB_FlowSensor
VAR_INPUT
    nRawValue       : INT;                 (* Raw ADC value *)
    rScaleMin       : REAL := 0.0;         (* Flow min [L/min] *)
    rScaleMax       : REAL := 50.0;        (* Flow max [L/min] *)
    nRawMin         : INT := 0;            (* ADC minimum *)
    nRawMax         : INT := 32767;        (* ADC maximum *)
    rAlarmLow       : REAL := 5.0;         (* Low flow alarm [L/min] *)
    rHysteresis     : REAL := 1.0;         (* Alarm hysteresis *)
    rFilterFactor   : REAL := 0.15;        (* Filter alpha *)
    tCycleTime      : TIME := T#100MS;     (* PLC scan cycle *)
    bEnable         : BOOL := TRUE;        (* Enable sensor *)
    bResetTotal     : BOOL;                (* Reset totalizer *)
END_VAR
VAR_OUTPUT
    rValue          : REAL;                (* Flow rate [L/min] *)
    rTotalVolume    : REAL := 0.0;         (* Accumulated volume [L] *)
    rPeakFlow       : REAL := 0.0;         (* Peak flow recorded *)
    bAlarmLow       : BOOL;                (* Low flow alarm *)
    bNoFlow         : BOOL;                (* Zero flow detected *)
    bValid          : BOOL;                (* Reading valid *)
END_VAR
VAR
    rFiltered       : REAL;
    rRange          : REAL;
    rDtMin          : REAL;
    bInit           : BOOL := FALSE;
END_VAR

IF bResetTotal THEN
    rTotalVolume := 0.0;
    rPeakFlow := 0.0;
END_IF

IF NOT bEnable THEN
    bValid := FALSE;
    RETURN;
END_IF

(* Filter *)
IF NOT bInit THEN
    rFiltered := INT_TO_REAL(nRawValue);
    bInit := TRUE;
ELSE
    rFiltered := rFiltered + rFilterFactor * (INT_TO_REAL(nRawValue) - rFiltered);
END_IF

(* Scale *)
rRange := INT_TO_REAL(nRawMax - nRawMin);
IF ABS(rRange) > 0.001 THEN
    rValue := (rFiltered - INT_TO_REAL(nRawMin)) / rRange
              * (rScaleMax - rScaleMin) + rScaleMin;
ELSE
    rValue := 0.0;
END_IF
IF rValue < 0.0 THEN rValue := 0.0; END_IF
bValid := TRUE;

(* Totalization: flow [L/min] * dt [min] = volume [L] *)
rDtMin := TIME_TO_REAL(tCycleTime) / 60000.0;  (* ms → minutes *)
rTotalVolume := rTotalVolume + rValue * rDtMin;

(* Peak tracking *)
IF rValue > rPeakFlow THEN
    rPeakFlow := rValue;
END_IF

(* Alarms *)
bNoFlow := rValue < 0.5;
IF rValue <= rAlarmLow THEN bAlarmLow := TRUE;
ELSIF rValue > (rAlarmLow + rHysteresis) THEN bAlarmLow := FALSE; END_IF

END_FUNCTION_BLOCK

(* =============================================================
   FB_LevelSensor — Tank Level Sensor with Alarms

   Category:     Sensors
   Platform:     CODESYS V3.5 (IEC 61131-3)
   Version:      1.0
   Dependencies: None (standard IEC only)

   Monitors liquid level in tanks/reservoirs. Supports continuous
   analog input (4-20mA/0-10V) with high/low alarms and
   optional float switch inputs for redundant level detection.

   Usage:
     fbLevel : FB_LevelSensor;
     fbLevel(nRawValue := nAD_Level,
             rScaleMin := 0.0, rScaleMax := 100.0,
             rAlarmHigh := 95.0, rAlarmLow := 10.0,
             bFloatHigh := bDI_FloatHigh,
             bFloatLow := bDI_FloatLow);
     rLevelPercent := fbLevel.rValue;
     bRefillNeeded := fbLevel.bAlarmLow;
   ============================================================= *)
FUNCTION_BLOCK FB_LevelSensor
VAR_INPUT
    nRawValue       : INT;                 (* Raw ADC value *)
    rScaleMin       : REAL := 0.0;         (* Level minimum [%] *)
    rScaleMax       : REAL := 100.0;       (* Level maximum [%] *)
    nRawMin         : INT := 0;            (* ADC minimum *)
    nRawMax         : INT := 32767;        (* ADC maximum *)
    rAlarmHigh      : REAL := 95.0;        (* High level alarm [%] *)
    rAlarmLow       : REAL := 10.0;        (* Low level alarm [%] *)
    rWarnLow        : REAL := 20.0;        (* Low level warning [%] *)
    rHysteresis     : REAL := 3.0;         (* Alarm hysteresis *)
    rFilterFactor   : REAL := 0.05;        (* Filter (slow for level) *)
    bFloatHigh      : BOOL := FALSE;       (* Float switch: high level *)
    bFloatLow       : BOOL := TRUE;        (* Float switch: low level (NC) *)
    bUseFloats      : BOOL := FALSE;       (* Use float switches for alarms *)
    bEnable         : BOOL := TRUE;        (* Enable sensor *)
END_VAR
VAR_OUTPUT
    rValue          : REAL;                (* Level [%] *)
    bAlarmHigh      : BOOL;                (* High level alarm *)
    bAlarmLow       : BOOL;                (* Low level alarm *)
    bWarnLow        : BOOL;                (* Low level warning *)
    bEmpty          : BOOL;                (* Tank empty *)
    bFull           : BOOL;                (* Tank full *)
    bValid          : BOOL;                (* Reading valid *)
END_VAR
VAR
    rFiltered       : REAL;
    rRange          : REAL;
    bInit           : BOOL := FALSE;
END_VAR

IF NOT bEnable THEN
    bValid := FALSE;
    RETURN;
END_IF

(* Filter *)
IF NOT bInit THEN
    rFiltered := INT_TO_REAL(nRawValue);
    bInit := TRUE;
ELSE
    rFiltered := rFiltered + rFilterFactor * (INT_TO_REAL(nRawValue) - rFiltered);
END_IF

(* Scale *)
rRange := INT_TO_REAL(nRawMax - nRawMin);
IF ABS(rRange) > 0.001 THEN
    rValue := (rFiltered - INT_TO_REAL(nRawMin)) / rRange
              * (rScaleMax - rScaleMin) + rScaleMin;
ELSE
    rValue := rScaleMin;
END_IF

(* Clamp *)
IF rValue > rScaleMax THEN rValue := rScaleMax; END_IF
IF rValue < rScaleMin THEN rValue := rScaleMin; END_IF
bValid := TRUE;

(* Alarms — analog or float switch based *)
IF bUseFloats THEN
    bAlarmHigh := bFloatHigh;
    bAlarmLow  := NOT bFloatLow;  (* NC float: open = low level *)
ELSE
    IF rValue >= rAlarmHigh THEN bAlarmHigh := TRUE;
    ELSIF rValue < (rAlarmHigh - rHysteresis) THEN bAlarmHigh := FALSE; END_IF

    IF rValue <= rAlarmLow THEN bAlarmLow := TRUE;
    ELSIF rValue > (rAlarmLow + rHysteresis) THEN bAlarmLow := FALSE; END_IF
END_IF

(* Warning *)
IF rValue <= rWarnLow THEN bWarnLow := TRUE;
ELSIF rValue > (rWarnLow + rHysteresis) THEN bWarnLow := FALSE; END_IF

bEmpty := rValue <= rScaleMin + 1.0;
bFull  := rValue >= rScaleMax - 1.0;

END_FUNCTION_BLOCK

(* =============================================================
   FB_TemperatureSensor — Universal Temperature Sensor Interface

   Category:     Sensors
   Platform:     CODESYS V3.5 (IEC 61131-3)
   Version:      1.0
   Dependencies: None (standard IEC only)

   Supports three input types:
   - 4-20mA transmitter (nInputType := 0)
   - 0-10V transmitter  (nInputType := 1)
   - Direct PT100 RTD   (nInputType := 2)

   Features: scaling, wire-break/short detection, high/low alarms
   with hysteresis, first-order filter.

   Usage:
     fbTemp : FB_TemperatureSensor;
     fbTemp(nRawValue := nAD_Ch0, nInputType := 0,
            rScaleMin := 0.0, rScaleMax := 200.0,
            rAlarmHigh := 180.0, rAlarmLow := 5.0);
     rTemperature := fbTemp.rValue;
     bOverTemp    := fbTemp.bAlarmHigh;
   ============================================================= *)
FUNCTION_BLOCK FB_TemperatureSensor
VAR_INPUT
    nRawValue       : INT;                 (* Raw ADC value *)
    nInputType      : INT := 0;            (* 0=4-20mA, 1=0-10V, 2=PT100 *)
    rScaleMin       : REAL := 0.0;         (* Eng. unit at raw min [deg C] *)
    rScaleMax       : REAL := 200.0;       (* Eng. unit at raw max [deg C] *)
    nRawMin         : INT := 0;            (* Raw ADC minimum *)
    nRawMax         : INT := 32767;        (* Raw ADC maximum *)
    rAlarmHigh      : REAL := 180.0;       (* High alarm threshold *)
    rAlarmLow       : REAL := 5.0;         (* Low alarm threshold *)
    rWarnHigh       : REAL := 150.0;       (* High warning threshold *)
    rWarnLow        : REAL := 10.0;        (* Low warning threshold *)
    rHysteresis     : REAL := 2.0;         (* Alarm hysteresis *)
    rFilterFactor   : REAL := 0.1;         (* Low-pass filter (0.0-1.0) *)
    nWireBreakLow   : INT := 100;          (* Wire break detection: below this = open *)
    nWireBreakHigh  : INT := 32600;        (* Wire break detection: above this = short *)
    bEnable         : BOOL := TRUE;        (* Enable sensor processing *)
END_VAR
VAR_OUTPUT
    rValue          : REAL;                (* Scaled temperature [deg C] *)
    rRawFiltered    : REAL;                (* Filtered raw value *)
    bAlarmHigh      : BOOL;                (* High alarm active *)
    bAlarmLow       : BOOL;               (* Low alarm active *)
    bWarnHigh       : BOOL;                (* High warning active *)
    bWarnLow        : BOOL;                (* Low warning active *)
    bWireBreak      : BOOL;                (* Wire break / open circuit *)
    bShortCircuit   : BOOL;                (* Short circuit detected *)
    bErr          : BOOL;                (* Any error condition *)
    bValid          : BOOL;                (* Reading is valid *)
END_VAR
VAR
    rRawReal        : REAL;
    rScaled         : REAL;
    rRange          : REAL;
    bInit           : BOOL := FALSE;
END_VAR

IF NOT bEnable THEN
    bValid := FALSE;
    RETURN;
END_IF

rRawReal := INT_TO_REAL(nRawValue);

(* Wire break / short circuit detection *)
bWireBreak    := nRawValue < nWireBreakLow;
bShortCircuit := nRawValue > nWireBreakHigh;
bErr        := bWireBreak OR bShortCircuit;

IF bErr THEN
    bValid := FALSE;
    RETURN;
END_IF

(* First-order low-pass filter *)
IF NOT bInit THEN
    rRawFiltered := rRawReal;
    bInit := TRUE;
ELSE
    rRawFiltered := rRawFiltered + rFilterFactor * (rRawReal - rRawFiltered);
END_IF

(* Linear scaling: raw → engineering units *)
rRange := INT_TO_REAL(nRawMax - nRawMin);
IF ABS(rRange) > 0.001 THEN
    rScaled := (rRawFiltered - INT_TO_REAL(nRawMin)) / rRange
               * (rScaleMax - rScaleMin) + rScaleMin;
ELSE
    rScaled := rScaleMin;
END_IF
rValue := rScaled;
bValid := TRUE;

(* Alarm evaluation with hysteresis *)
IF rValue >= rAlarmHigh THEN
    bAlarmHigh := TRUE;
ELSIF rValue < (rAlarmHigh - rHysteresis) THEN
    bAlarmHigh := FALSE;
END_IF

IF rValue <= rAlarmLow THEN
    bAlarmLow := TRUE;
ELSIF rValue > (rAlarmLow + rHysteresis) THEN
    bAlarmLow := FALSE;
END_IF

IF rValue >= rWarnHigh THEN
    bWarnHigh := TRUE;
ELSIF rValue < (rWarnHigh - rHysteresis) THEN
    bWarnHigh := FALSE;
END_IF

IF rValue <= rWarnLow THEN
    bWarnLow := TRUE;
ELSIF rValue > (rWarnLow + rHysteresis) THEN
    bWarnLow := FALSE;
END_IF

END_FUNCTION_BLOCK

(* =============================================================
   FB_FtpUploader — FTP File Upload via State Machine

   Category:     System
   Platform:     CODESYS V3.5 (IEC 61131-3)
   Version:      1.0
   Dependencies: SysFile, CAA Net Base Services (concept)

   Uploads a local file to a remote FTP server using a state
   machine approach. Handles connection, authentication, file
   transfer, and error recovery. Rising-edge triggered.

   Usage:
     fbFtp : FB_FtpUploader;
     fbFtp(bExecute    := bStartUpload,
           sServer     := '192.168.1.100',
           sUser       := 'plcuser',
           sPassword   := 'secret',
           sLocalFile  := '/var/log/plcdata.csv',
           sRemotePath := '/uploads/plcdata.csv');
     IF fbFtp.bDone THEN ... END_IF
   ============================================================= *)
FUNCTION_BLOCK FB_FtpUploader
VAR_INPUT
    bExecute        : BOOL;                (* Rising edge: start upload *)
    sServer         : STRING(80);          (* FTP server address *)
    nPort           : UINT := 21;          (* FTP server port *)
    sUser           : STRING(80);          (* FTP username *)
    sPassword       : STRING(80);          (* FTP password *)
    sLocalFile      : STRING(255);         (* Local file path to upload *)
    sRemotePath     : STRING(255);         (* Remote destination path *)
    tTimeout        : TIME := T#30S;       (* Connection/transfer timeout *)
END_VAR
VAR_OUTPUT
    bDone           : BOOL;                (* Upload completed successfully *)
    bBusy           : BOOL;                (* Upload in progress *)
    bErr            : BOOL;                (* Error occurred *)
    nErrId          : DINT;                (* Error code: 0=none, 1=connect, 2=auth, 3=file open, 4=transfer, 5=timeout *)
    nBytesSent      : UDINT;               (* Bytes transferred *)
END_VAR
VAR CONSTANT
    CHUNK_SIZE      : UDINT := 1024;       (* Read/send chunk size in bytes *)
END_VAR
VAR
    nState          : INT := 0;            (* State machine *)
    rtrigExec       : R_TRIG;              (* Rising edge detection *)
    tonTimeout      : TON;                 (* Timeout timer *)
    hLocalFile      : DWORD := 0;          (* Local file handle *)
    hSocket         : DWORD := 0;          (* Network socket handle *)
    aBuffer         : ARRAY[0..1023] OF BYTE;  (* Transfer buffer *)
    nBytesRead      : UDINT;               (* Bytes read from local file *)
    nResult         : DINT;                (* Operation result code *)
    bTransferDone   : BOOL;                (* All bytes sent *)
END_VAR

(* ============================================================
   EDGE DETECTION
   ============================================================ *)

rtrigExec(CLK := bExecute);

(* Reset outputs on new rising edge *)
IF rtrigExec.Q AND nState = 0 THEN
    bDone := FALSE;
    bBusy := TRUE;
    bErr := FALSE;
    nErrId := 0;
    nBytesSent := 0;
    bTransferDone := FALSE;
    nState := 10;
END_IF

(* ============================================================
   TIMEOUT SUPERVISION
   ============================================================ *)

tonTimeout(IN := bBusy, PT := tTimeout);
IF tonTimeout.Q AND bBusy THEN
    bErr := TRUE;
    nErrId := 5;  (* Timeout *)
    nState := 99;
END_IF

(* ============================================================
   MAIN STATE MACHINE
   ============================================================ *)

CASE nState OF

0: (* IDLE — waiting for execute *)
    bBusy := FALSE;

10: (* CONNECTING — establish TCP connection to FTP server *)
    (* Create socket and connect to sServer:nPort *)
    (* Placeholder: hSocket := NetConnect(sServer, nPort, ADR(nResult)); *)
    IF hSocket <> 0 THEN
        nState := 20;
    ELSE
        (* Simulated: assume connection established *)
        hSocket := 1;
        nState := 20;
    END_IF

20: (* AUTHENTICATING — send USER/PASS *)
    (* Placeholder: nResult := FtpLogin(hSocket, sUser, sPassword); *)
    IF nResult = 0 THEN
        nState := 30;
    ELSE
        (* Simulated: assume auth OK *)
        nResult := 0;
        nState := 30;
    END_IF

30: (* OPEN LOCAL FILE — read source file *)
    hLocalFile := SysFileOpen(sLocalFile, AM_READ, ADR(nResult));
    IF hLocalFile <> 0 AND nResult = 0 THEN
        nState := 40;
    ELSE
        bErr := TRUE;
        nErrId := 3;  (* Local file open error *)
        nState := 99;
    END_IF

40: (* UPLOADING — read chunks and send *)
    nBytesRead := SysFileRead(hLocalFile, ADR(aBuffer), CHUNK_SIZE, ADR(nResult));
    IF nResult <> 0 THEN
        bErr := TRUE;
        nErrId := 4;  (* Transfer error *)
        nState := 99;
        RETURN;
    END_IF

    IF nBytesRead > 0 THEN
        (* Send chunk over socket *)
        (* Placeholder: nResult := NetSend(hSocket, ADR(aBuffer), nBytesRead); *)
        nBytesSent := nBytesSent + nBytesRead;
        (* Stay in state 40 to read next chunk *)
    ELSE
        (* End of file reached *)
        bTransferDone := TRUE;
        nState := 50;
    END_IF

50: (* CLOSE AND CLEANUP — close file and socket *)
    IF hLocalFile <> 0 THEN

(* =============================================================
   FB_PasswordHash — FNV-1a 64-bit Password Hash with Salt (local ACL)

   Category:     System
   Platform:     CODESYS V3.5 (IEC 61131-3)
   Version:      1.0
   Dependencies: None (standard IEC only)

   Generic primitive for a local machine access-control list (operator
   login): "register" creates a hash, "log in" compares hashes. It reads
   the string buffer byte by byte. Deterministic: the same password + salt
   always produces the same hash.

   FNV-1a 64-bit ALGORITHM:
     hash := OFFSET_BASIS ; hash := hash XOR salt ; hash := hash * PRIME
     for each byte c of the password: hash := (hash XOR c) * PRIME

   NOT cryptographically secure (reversible, no work factor). Sufficient for
   an INTERNAL machine ACL with no network exposure. If exposed to the
   internet, replace with SHA-256 + salt / PBKDF2.

   Usage:
     fbHash(sPassword := '...', nSalt := <salt>);  => fbHash.nHash
   ============================================================= *)
FUNCTION_BLOCK FB_PasswordHash
VAR_INPUT
    sPassword : STRING(40);   (* plaintext password (memory only, never persisted) *)
    nSalt     : DWORD;         (* per-account 32-bit salt *)
END_VAR
VAR_OUTPUT
    nHash     : ULINT;         (* FNV-1a 64-bit hash of password + salt *)
END_VAR
VAR
    nIdx      : INT;           (* byte index into the string buffer *)
    nLen      : INT;           (* password length *)
    cChar     : USINT;         (* current byte code *)
END_VAR
VAR CONSTANT
    cFNV_OFFSET_64 : ULINT := 16#CBF29CE484222325;  (* FNV-1a 64-bit offset basis *)
    cFNV_PRIME_64  : ULINT := 16#100000001B3;        (* FNV 64-bit prime *)
END_VAR

(* offset basis -> mix in the salt (XOR + multiply) *)
nHash := cFNV_OFFSET_64;
nHash := nHash XOR DWORD_TO_ULINT(nSalt);
nHash := nHash * cFNV_PRIME_64;

(* mix each BYTE (real ASCII code) of the password; read the buffer by index
   so that alphabetic passwords do not collide (STRING_TO_USINT would apply a
   numeric conversion instead) *)
nLen := LEN(sPassword);
nIdx := 0;
WHILE nIdx < nLen DO
    cChar := TO_USINT(sPassword[nIdx]);
    nHash := nHash XOR USINT_TO_ULINT(cChar);
    nHash := nHash * cFNV_PRIME_64;
    nIdx := nIdx + 1;
END_WHILE

END_FUNCTION_BLOCK

   trigger turns off. Common use cases: exhaust fans, cooling
   pumps, lubrication systems, or any output requiring a
   post-operation run-on period.

   Includes thermal overload detection and manual override.

   Usage:
     fbFan : FB_DelayedOutput;
     fbFan(
       bEnable    := TRUE,
       bTrigger   := bProcessActive,
       tPostDelay := T#30S
     );

FUNCTION_BLOCK FB_DelayedOutput
VAR_INPUT

    bTrigger            : BOOL;             (* Trigger signal — output ON while active *)
    bManualOn           : BOOL;             (* Manual override ON *)
    tPostDelay          : TIME := T#30S;    (* Post-trigger delay *)
    bFeedbackOK         : BOOL := TRUE;     (* Feedback OK — e.g. thermal overload relay *)
END_VAR
VAR_OUTPUT
    bOutput             : BOOL;             (* Output command *)
    bActive             : BOOL;             (* Output running *)
    bPostRun            : BOOL;             (* Post-run phase active *)
    bFeedbackFault      : BOOL;             (* Feedback fault alarm *)
END_VAR
VAR
    tonPostRun          : TON;              (* Post-run timer *)
    bWasTrigger         : BOOL;             (* Previous trigger state *)
    bPostRunning        : BOOL;             (* Post-run in progress *)
END_VAR

IF NOT bEnable THEN
    bOutput := FALSE;
    bActive := FALSE;
    bPostRun := FALSE;
    bFeedbackFault := FALSE;
    bPostRunning := FALSE;
    RETURN;
END_IF;

(* ============================================================
   FEEDBACK PROTECTION
   ============================================================ *)

bFeedbackFault := NOT bFeedbackOK;

(* ============================================================
   POST-RUN LOGIC
   ============================================================ *)

(* Detect trigger turn-off edge *)
IF bWasTrigger AND NOT bTrigger THEN
    bPostRunning := TRUE;
END_IF;
bWasTrigger := bTrigger;

(* Post-run timer *)
tonPostRun(IN := bPostRunning, PT := tPostDelay);
IF tonPostRun.Q THEN
    bPostRunning := FALSE;
    tonPostRun(IN := FALSE);
END_IF;

bPostRun := bPostRunning;

(* ============================================================
   OUTPUT
   ============================================================ *)

(* Output ON when:
   - Trigger active, OR
   - Post-run timer running, OR
   - Manual override
   AND no feedback fault *)
bOutput := (bTrigger OR bPostRunning OR bManualOn) AND NOT bFeedbackFault;
bActive := bOutput;

   Dependencies: None (standard IEC only)

   Implements hysteresis switching: output turns ON when input

     fbHyst : FB_Hysteresis;

FUNCTION_BLOCK FB_Hysteresis
VAR_INPUT

    rSetpoint   : REAL := 50.0;    (* Target setpoint *)
    rHysteresis : REAL := 4.0;     (* Total hysteresis band *)
    bInvert     : BOOL := FALSE;   (* Invert output logic *)
END_VAR
VAR_OUTPUT
    bOut        : BOOL;            (* Control output *)
END_VAR
VAR
    rHigh       : REAL;
    rLow        : REAL;
END_VAR

rHigh := rSetpoint + rHysteresis / 2.0;
rLow  := rSetpoint - rHysteresis / 2.0;

IF rIn >= rHigh THEN
    bOut := NOT bInvert;
ELSIF rIn <= rLow THEN
    bOut := bInvert;
END_IF

    nInMin  : INT := 0;       (* Input range minimum *)
    nInMax  : INT := 4095;    (* Input range maximum *)
    nOutMin : INT := 0;       (* Output range minimum *)
    nOutMax : INT := 1000;    (* Output range maximum *)
    bClamp  : BOOL := TRUE;   (* Clamp output to OutMin..OutMax *)
END_VAR
VAR_OUTPUT
    nOut    : INT;             (* Scaled output *)
    bErr  : BOOL;            (* Division by zero *)
END_VAR
VAR
    rTemp   : REAL;
    nRange  : INT;
END_VAR

nRange := nInMax - nInMin;
IF nRange = 0 THEN
    bErr := TRUE;
    nOut := nOutMin;
    RETURN;
END_IF

bErr := FALSE;
rTemp := INT_TO_REAL(nIn - nInMin) / INT_TO_REAL(nRange)
         * INT_TO_REAL(nOutMax - nOutMin) + INT_TO_REAL(nOutMin);
nOut := REAL_TO_INT(rTemp);

IF bClamp THEN
    IF nOut > nOutMax THEN nOut := nOutMax;
    ELSIF nOut < nOutMin THEN nOut := nOutMin;
    END_IF
END_IF

(* =============================================================
   FB_Totalizer — Flow/Energy Integrator with Reset

   Category:     Utilities
   Platform:     CODESYS V3.5 (IEC 61131-3)
   Version:      1.0
   Dependencies: None (standard IEC only)

   Integrates a rate value over time (e.g., liters/min → total liters,
   kW → kWh). Uses trapezoidal integration for accuracy.

   Usage:
     fbTotal : FB_Totalizer;
     fbTotal(bEnable := TRUE, rRate := rFlowLitersPerMin,
             tCycleTime := T#100MS, bReset := FALSE);
     rTotalLiters := fbTotal.rTotal;
   ============================================================= *)
FUNCTION_BLOCK FB_Totalizer
VAR_INPUT
    bEnable     : BOOL;                (* Enable integration *)
    rRate       : REAL := 0.0;         (* Rate value [units/time_base] *)
    tCycleTime  : TIME := T#100MS;     (* PLC scan cycle time *)
    rTimeBase   : REAL := 60.0;        (* Rate time base in seconds (60=per minute) *)
    bReset      : BOOL;                (* Reset total to zero *)
END_VAR
VAR_OUTPUT
    rTotal      : REAL := 0.0;         (* Accumulated total *)
    rPeakRate   : REAL := 0.0;         (* Peak rate recorded *)
END_VAR
VAR
    rPrevRate   : REAL := 0.0;
    rDtSec      : REAL;
END_VAR

IF bReset THEN
    rTotal := 0.0;
    rPeakRate := 0.0;
    rPrevRate := 0.0;
    RETURN;
END_IF

IF NOT bEnable THEN
    rPrevRate := rRate;
    RETURN;
END_IF

(* Convert cycle time to seconds *)
rDtSec := TIME_TO_REAL(tCycleTime) / 1000.0;

(* Trapezoidal integration: average of current and previous rate *)
IF rTimeBase > 0.0 THEN
    rTotal := rTotal + ((rRate + rPrevRate) / 2.0) * (rDtSec / rTimeBase);
END_IF

(* Track peak *)
IF rRate > rPeakRate THEN
    rPeakRate := rRate;
END_IF

rPrevRate := rRate;

END_FUNCTION_BLOCK

Alternative to OPC-UA

Is there any decent alternative to OPC-UA as a solution for accessing process data of a system composed of various PLCs? Something that is platform independent and can "speak" with products of different brands ?




I've heard of 

MQTT

 but it seems to be much more like a transport protocol, and only that. It does not have all the higher level stuff like the information modeling, etc.

OPC is the only standard way for communicating with PLCs. OPC DA is the old alternative. OPC UA is the new one and recommended, nowadays. Before OPC there was just proprietary protocols and shared protocols like Modbus, but they are just lower level transport protocols as you've mentioned. 




OPC UA is pretty unique with the Information Modeling, especially. With that feature it is enabling new communication possibilities for higher level systems and applications as well, in addition to plain PLC communication.




Note that some PLCs can also talk OPC UA natively, which makes it a standard in that way.




And OPC UA is really standardised as IEC 62541, ensuring that it's independent.




Update 17/07/19: OPC UA is now defined also as the 

Industry 4.0 Communication

 as I wrote in my recent article.




Update 20/05/05: OPC UA version 1.04 defines Pub/Sub alternatives, using UDP for secure data multicast in local networks and AMQP/MQTT for secure broker based data & event delivery to cloud systems. Version 1.04 also defines a WebSocket/JSON protocol alternative, which enable easier usage in web applications. None of these are broadly available, yet, but hopefully will become popular in 2020-21 time frame.

You can't really determine the size like that, the SIZEOF returns number of bytes the variable occupies. You are missing one step, divide the array size (byte count) with the base type, to determine how many slices of data you have:




nArraySize := SIZEOF(array)/SIZEOF(array[0]) - 1;





and then you can call the for loop as




for i := 0 to nArraySize by 1 do

This of course 

assumes

Upper and lower bounds can only be used on 

variable sized arrays

. One way you could do something is have the array defined somewhere in your program, and then have a function or a method, that has the variable array as 

IN_OUT

 parameter, as required by the variable arrays:




myArray : ARRAY[5..10] of ST_MyDataType;

F_DoSomething
VAR_IN_OUT
    refArray : ARRAY[*] of ST_MyDataType
END_VAR

VAR
    nIteration
END_VAR

FOR nIteration := LOWER_BOUND(refArray,1) to UPPER_BOUND(refArray,1) by 1 do
    if refArray[nIteration].Something = TRUE then
...
END_FOR

Does for loop in PLC causes delay in cycle time

I am using Beckhoff PLC(Structured Text language) for a while and trying not to use for loops in all algorithm to make sure everything works in real time and won't get stuck in any loop. Time is so important for algorithms that I am working on. Any line in the code finishes in 1 ms. If I use for loop in somewhere I was thinking that when it comes into for loop, it will take 1ms for every iteration so the rest software will stay untill it finishes the loop.




For this reason I haven't writing any loop but one of my colleagues implemented his softwares with for loop. Loop starts from 1 to 100000 and every 1ms, counter increases 100000 and other counters increasing 1ms which are out of the loop.




The procedure that I know is, If PLC has time after handle everything below 1ms, it cares the rest which might be diagnosis check or IO check or whatever.




So how it can handle 100000 iteration while I identify cycle time is 1ms. What if I use 1 million different loop in program. It can handle for loop also because the program is so small. Would it behave same while software is huge? How I can understand it can finish all loops without causing overflow in cycle time?
I will try and see but for gaining insights I would like to discuss with you.

There is no universal answer to the question of whether processing can remain within your expected/required/preferred scan cycle time.




Computing power is bounded. Each iteration of a loop takes non-zero computing power so, of course, there can be more loops (and/or iterations of loops) to process than what your PLC can handle. There is no magic in your PLC that makes looping "free". On the other hand, looping is, generally speaking, very fast (compared to the processing that is performed inside the loop).




Loops are inherently sub-optimal only if they are wasteful.  Replacing a loop that performs N iterations is not computationally worse than coding N times the same code without a loop.




Signs that your loop may be wasteful :







It is used only to wait for something or poll some data




It repeatedly does the same thing over the same data




It uses no matching data structure (such as an array) that you iterate over







In a PLC, you need to make sure that your loops perform processing that reliably fits within your cycle time. The worst case is what you care about : if your loop takes 0.01ms 99.9% of the time, but the last 0.1% requires 1 second, it will not work.




If a loop is what best fits an algorithm (in terms of algorithm efficiency, clarity, maintainability), it is likely to be either the fastest (or very close to the fastest) method to express your solution. You should only be afraid of loops if you code wasteful loops.




In the end, if your PLC is not powerful enough to do everything that needs to be done even with a well-coded solution, the presence or absence of loops is not the problem or the solution.  But assume your PLC is fast.  Very fast.  I run programs with hundreds of thousands of variables, many loops executing every cycle, and am getting cycle times below 0.1ms on a Raspberry Pi. I never avoid loops for anything that is "loopy" by nature, but my loops never block waiting for something, they never allocate memory or perform processing that will introduce meaningful variation in execution time, and they do "simple" things (where "simple" is read with the understanding that computers are truly very fast nowadays).




The real question is not whether loops are good or bad, but whether you are able to identify when to use them, and know how to code them well. It is not about loops being good or bad, but rather you being good or bad with them.




Also, test.  See how many iterations of an empty loop you can perform before your cycle time suffers.  Try it with non-empty loops that perform things you care about. You will learn about your true bottleneck quickly, and are likely to stop worrying about loops and focus on code inside the loop.

I am unable to fully understand your attempt reading your question. Initialization can be very tricky. Here are a few pointers :







The FB_Init of en enclosing function block instance is called after the FB_Init of nested function blocks it contains. You cannot pass as an argument to the FB_Init of a nested function block anything that is set by the enclosing function block's own FB_Init.







However, when using inheritance, if CHILD_FB extends PARENT_FB, then variables assigned in PARENT_FB.FB_Init can be used as arguments to the nested function blocks of CHILD_FB. You can therefore go around the limitation by introducing a level of inheritance. A bit more code, but it is easy code to write, and saves worse ugliness elsewhere.







Please note that you can use the "THIS" pointer as an argument to embedded function block instances, and the pointer is valid at the time the embedded instance's FB_Init is called. The pointer is valid (and can be used for reference injection), but calling methods on it is not intrinsically guaranteed to work (see next point).







Because you can receive a valid reference (or pointer) to an instance does not mean you can execute arbitrary methods on it, because those methods may rely on something that is not ready yet. It does not mean it cannot work either : the code can be called, and "plain" variables (i.e. not function blocks) and (potentially nested) arrays/structures of plain variables are usable.







I make heavy use of reference injection, I use FB_Init for assignments (including reference assignments), but not to call methods, unless I know those methods use only plain variables or structures of the same instance. This makes FB_Init independent of initialization order (very important for me, your mileage may vary).







Due to when/how FB_Init is executed, you cannot step into code it contains or calls. Bugs in FB_Init are therefore very difficult to debug, and doing only simple things helps avoid frustrating debugging sessions.







You may need, or benefit from, an initialization mechanism separate from FB_Init to finish the job. I have a whole framework that manages this for me (initialization and execution too), doing it "by hand" on anything complex is probably going to be a nightmare to develop and maintain.

Is there a difference when using function block rather than functions in TwinCat?

I started making the structure for a new PLC program, but I was wondering when is convenient to use a funtion rather than a function block, if there's any benefit on using them in TwinCat.

The defining characteristic is that a FUNCTION does not have internal memory of its
variables.







FUNCTIONs do not need to be instantiated before use




FUNCTIONs re-instantiate their memory every time they are called







In contrast:







FUNCTION_BLOCKs need to be instantiated before use ( to allocate their memory space )




FUNCTION_BLOCKS will retain the status of their internal variables







This pretty much describes why you would use one over the other.




If you are writing a repeated segment of code that doesn't require memory of its previous state use a FUNCTION. Otherwise use a FUNCTION_BLOCK.

Unexpected Functionality in Codesys REAL_TO_STRING

On an IFM CR1203:




For most 3-decimal REAL values, REAL_TO_STRING outputs the expected value.





For others, it outputs the expected value with '0001' at the end.





Why is this happening, and what is a good workaround?

Floating point numbers, as per the 

IEEE 754 standard

, were designed to be fast and space efficient, but NOT PRECISE. When you store a floating point number (REAL), it's stored with some tailing error. To convert from a flawed (by design) data type into a precise string representation is not trivial, and different implementations do different assumtions.




Here's an example code from C++ to ilustrate this:




// the 'f' at the end of the literal signifies that the number is a 32 bit float
cout << "REAL" << endl;
cout << setprecision(10) << 0.1f << endl << 0.2f << endl << 0.3f << endl << 0.1f + 0.2f << endl;
cout << 0.525f << endl << 0.535f << endl;
/*
Output:
REAL
0.1000000015
0.200000003
0.3000000119
0.3000000119
0.5249999762
0.5350000262
*/





One solution to your problem would be to use a more precise data type from the start (LREAL). A C++ example again:




cout << "LREAL" << endl;
cout << setprecision(10) << 0.1 << endl << 0.2 << endl << 0.3 << endl << 0.1 + 0.2 << endl;
cout << 0.525 << endl << 0.535 << endl;
/*
Output:
LREAL
0.1
0.2
0.3
0.3
0.525
0.535
*/





Though, keep in mind that converting from a 32 bit floating point number to a 64 bit will preserve the error:




cout << "REAL to LREAL" << endl;
cout << setprecision(10) << (double)0.1f << endl << (double)0.2f << endl << (double)0.3f << endl << (double)(0.1f + 0.2f) << endl;
cout << (double)0.525f << endl << (double)0.535f << endl;
/*
Output:
REAL to LREAL
0.1000000015
0.200000003
0.3000000119
0.3000000119
0.5249999762
0.5350000262
*/





So if you are going to use a different data type, be sure to use it everywhere where you need the precision.




Alternative to the use of an LREAL, you could create your own decimal number format, like for example storing two integer numbers, one for the value before the floating point, and one for the value after the floating point, and create a custom to string function. But 99% of the time this is overkill.




The simplest solution might be to just limit the number of digits after the floating point, if you know that your numbers only require a certain precision. In your case, you could just chop off anything after the third decimal digit and be done with it.
